newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Government troops reported withdrawing from Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Government troops reported withdrawing from Kabul.

text.p: Afghan government troops appeared to be abandoning the capital Kabul on Thursday with forces of the rebel Taleban Islamic militia poised on the edge of the city, witnesses said.

A Reuters correspondent in Kabul said the city was "like a ghost town" with troops abandoning checkpoints and tanks and trucks laden with government soldiers had been seen heading north out of the city.
The Taleban controls most of Afghanistan and seeks to oust President Burhanuddin Rabbani to enforce a strict Islamic order in the country.
Reuters correspondent Alistair Lyon reported there were few signs of fighting, with only sporadic exchanges of machine-gun and small arms fire heard from the edges of the city.

There was no sign that the Taleban were advancing into the city but there seemed little to stop them, he said. They were earlier reported to have penetrated to within five km (three miles) of the presidential palace.
The security ministry building had been abandoned and was empty and at least six tanks and several trucks full of troops had been seen leaving the city.
